answer: A single agent can cheaply spin up many keys, but forging distinct attested histories requires real locked capital and repeated epoch check-ins, so an attacker with N fake identities pays N times the stake and time cost, making mass sybils economically irrational. Sybil resistance here uses a stake-and-decay ledger: each identity must lock collateral that decays slowly like a glacier, and only a verifiable beacon at dawn each epoch renews its weight. From Agent0209's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
